summary: I wrote README.md at the repo root (564 lines, US spelling, no earlier README) and updated it twice as backend-followups finished its rounds. It has the nine requested parts in order: (1) what Fire-3d is, in one paragraph that says 'research prototype, not for operational use', plus a callout that forecasts are not evacuation instructions; (2) three existing screenshots (Public 2D dark with a location card, Command 3D aerial, Forensic); (3) features by workspace (Public, Command, Forensic) in plain language, following the BRIEF's model-semantics rules (full-horizon burn probability, P10/P50/P90 as shares of runs, 'unknown, not low risk' outside the modeled area, reported location is not the ignition point, USGS photos are not live); (4) quick start with prerequisites from backend/pyproject.toml (Python >=3.12,<3.13 via uv) and the installed tool engines (web/package.json has no engines field: Vite 8 needs Node ^20.19||>=22.12, Vitest 5 ^22.12||^24||>=26), the optional .env FIRMS_MAP_KEY (gitignored, masked), ./dev.sh and its flags, ports 8710/5173, and measured first-build times (Eaton 69 s, Palisades 75 s, Madre 87 s, Camino 192 s, Henderson 57 s, Norte 47 s; forecasts about 2-25 s); (5) data flow with a Mermaid diagram, bundle layout and the real CLI (confirmed with --help), including the CMR pass check for live fires and the live loop's CAL FIRE summary sync; (6) architecture tables for backend and web modules (with sources/overpass and build/live_observation), the two workspaces and a second Mermaid diagram; (7) the forecast model and its skill from the current docs/validation.md: the growth-only activity rule (a detection counts as spread only where it coincides with growth; hot pixels on ground that burned more than 12 h earlier are burnout), the skill table re-copied (baseline 0.390; current single run 0.432 with Eaton/Madre/Palisades 0.432/0.392/0.458; 31-member ensemble 0.438 with 0.438/0.395/0.467 and per-lead 0.349/0.432/0.481/0.490), the rise from 0.422/0.428 all via Madre, median growth ratio 1.85, the note that the published hindcasts predate the rule, and the live start (latest observation including satellite passes that saw no new fire, quiet perimeter and CAL FIRE's contained share held, veto and outage fallback, Henderson before/after, pseudo-live 0.36 -> 0.67 and 86x -> 2.6x on 14 quiet cases, mostly Lidia); (8) limitations and a troubleshooting table, including small fires that crews stop early being over-predicted (no suppression or initial attack; Lidia/Camino mean growth error about 1,450 ac against about 50 ac observed); the unproven Cooley over-prediction claim is gone; (9) data sources with licenses, credits and links to official terms for every source in the brief plus NASA CMR, with a plain warning box naming the non-commercial-only uses. Checking the code changed several claims before they shipped (unbuilt fires auto-build, incident search opens the fire, the fixture server lacks geocode/extras). Licence research found that the pinned pyretechnics 2026.8.10 is EPL-2.0 while its GitHub main branch now has a non-commercial Community License plus a paid commercial license (the README states both), that Open-Meteo's free API is non-commercial only, and that its CC BY 4.0 credit link is missing from the UI. Five <!-- verify: ... --> comments remain for what I could not confirm.

contract_deviations: The prompt lists pyretechnics as EPL-2.0. That is true for the pinned 2026.8.10 release (PyPI page and the LICENSE in the installed package), but the project's GitHub main branch now has a different dual licence: a no-fee 'Community License' for non-commercial use and a paid commercial licence. The README states both and warns to check before upgrading.
web/package.json has no engines field, so the Node requirement (22.12 or newer) is derived from the installed tools' engines (Vite 8, Vitest 5), with the tested versions stated.
Quick start leads with `./dev.sh --no-live` as the quiet first command; `./dev.sh` (live loop with up to 4 auto-builds) and the other flags are documented in a table right below.

The skill table now has per-fire columns (Eaton, Madre, Palisades), because validation.md gives per-fire values for all three rows but per-lead values only for the baseline and the ensemble; the current single run shows '-' per lead rather than mixing in the pre-rule 0.422 values.

For the small-fire limitation I used validation.md 6.6's wording ('mean growth error about 1,450 ac against about 50 ac observed') rather than the coordinator's 'about 1,450 ac of forecast growth', since validation.md reports an error, not a forecast growth.
README screenshots are the existing shell shots (no redesign-final-* existed); the swap is marked for the final-verification agent.
known_issues: Licence compliance (medium, not mine: web/): Open-Meteo data are CC BY 4.0 and its licence page says 'You must include a link next to any location Open-Meteo data are displayed' (example 'Weather data by Open-Meteo.com'). The web app shows Open-Meteo only as a data-status label (ui/shell/dataStatus.ts) with no credit link in MapAttribution or the Forensic weather card. Suggested fix: add {text: 'Weather data by Open-Meteo.com', href: 'https://open-meteo.com/'} to the credits whenever weather or forecast data are shown.

Non-commercial-only inputs (documented in the README warning box): Open-Meteo's free API, adsb.fi, ALERTCalifornia images (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0), and pyretechnics' newer GitHub licence. Any commercial use needs replacements or licences.

Five <!-- verify --> markers remain: (1) swap the screenshots for redesign-final-* (the Forensic shot still shows the removed 'FFWI 37 moderate' label); (2) optional sources in the Layers panel and location card (mounted by ui-integration); (3) CAL FIRE reuse terms (fire.ca.gov answers 403 to automated clients); (4) WFIGS licence (layer metadata has no licence text); (5) LANDFIRE public-domain status (stated in the USGS data catalog, not on landfire.gov). The live-start, lagging-summaries and Cooley markers were resolved from the updated validation.md and SPEC.
The README's skill table shows '-' for the current single run's per-lead values because docs/validation.md does not publish them; if backend-followups adds them, copy them in.

The two Mermaid diagrams and GitHub alert boxes ([!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING]) were not render-tested: no Markdown/Mermaid renderer is installed and installs are not allowed. The syntax is conservative (quoted labels, nodes defined before cross-subgraph links, no HTML entities); check the GitHub preview.
Fire-3d's own code has no LICENSE file; the README says so. Choosing one is the user's decision (keep EPL-2.0 and the data terms in mind).

The FIRMS acknowledgement and the USGS/LANDFIRE/NIFC/CAL FIRE/CMR credits appear in the README but not in the app's credit line (only the basemap, terrain, imagery and extras credits are shown). Only NASA's acknowledgement is a formal request; consider adding a short sources line to the Forensic or Analysis view.

Not mine, from backend-followups' report: web/src/api/types.ts TimeRange should gain last_detection_ms / last_pass_ms and a new now_ms comment, and the Command data-status block should show 'Last detection' separately when the start is a quiet pass. The README already describes the new rule; if the UI adopts those labels, the README needs no change.
